sentences.en: On one hand, players were hiding it from their opponents and from fans.
sentences.zh: 一方面，球员们对对手和球迷隐瞒此事。

sentences.en: On the other, everybody knew it was happening.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，大家都知道这事在发生。

sentences.en: One player, a Hall of Famer named Roger Swornsby, did an interview with True Magazine that was
sentences.zh: 一位名叫罗杰·斯旺斯比的棒球名人堂成员，曾接受《真实》杂志采访，

sentences.en: published under the headline,
sentences.zh: 文章标题是：

sentences.en: You've Got to Cheat to Win in Baseball.
sentences.zh: “在棒球比赛中，你必须作弊才能赢。”

sentences.en: Because of this ethical gray area, for years it went like this.
sentences.zh: 正因为这种道德灰色地带，多年来情况一直如此。

sentences.en: A team would be caught sign-stealing.
sentences.zh: 一支球队被抓到偷暗号。

sentences.en: The other team would say, hey, cut it out.
sentences.zh: 另一支球队会说，嘿，别干了。

sentences.en: And then they would come up with a new way of doing it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就会想出一种新的偷法。

sentences.en: For years, Major League Baseball did nothing.
sentences.zh: 多年来，美国职业棒球大联盟对此毫无作为。

sentences.en: But their view on sign-stealing changed after a technological breakthrough in the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 但他们在20世纪50年代经历了一次技术突破后，对偷暗号的看法改变了。

sentences.en: NBC had just invested in a camera with an 80-inch Spacemaster telephoto lens and unveiled it
sentences.zh: NBC当时刚投资了一台配备80英寸Spacemaster长焦镜头的摄像机，并将其

sentences.en: for a game of the week.
sentences.zh: 用于每周一场的比赛直播。

sentences.en: The broadcasters realized that they could now clearly see the catcher's signs and told
sentences.zh: 转播商意识到他们现在可以清晰地看到捕手的暗号，并告诉

sentences.en: the audience what was coming before each pitch.
sentences.zh: 观众在每次投球前会发生什么。

sentences.en: One of the people who happened to be watching the game that day was the commissioner, who
sentences.zh: 那天恰好在看比赛的人之一就是当时的专员，

sentences.en: was Ford Frick at the time.
sentences.zh: 也就是当时的福特·弗里克。

sentences.en: And he thought it was a horrible idea.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这主意糟透了。

sentences.en: He saw that he immediately went to NBC to agree not to use the camera again, ever.
sentences.zh: 他看到后立即找到NBC，要求他们再也不要使用那台摄像机。

sentences.en: If the guys in the booth could pick it up, the dugout could have the TV on.
sentences.zh: 如果转播间的人能看出来，那休息区的球队也能通过电视看出来。

sentences.en: In 1962, the commissioner took a baby step to discourage sign-stealing.
sentences.zh: 1962年，专员采取了一项初步措施来遏制偷暗号行为。

sentences.en: Frick said publicly that he would overturn any game if it was proven the winning team had
sentences.zh: 弗里克公开表示，如果证实获胜球队使用了机械手段偷暗号，

sentences.en: stolen signs using mechanical means, like a camera or a buzzer system, or even binoculars.
sentences.zh: 比如摄像机、蜂鸣器系统，甚至是望远镜，他将推翻比赛结果。

sentences.en: This was the line in the sand in terms of baseball ethics.
sentences.zh: 这是棒球道德方面划下的一条底线。

sentences.en: Players were allowed to steal with their eyes because that was considered a skill.
sentences.zh: 球员们被允许用眼睛偷暗号，因为那被视为一种技巧。

sentences.en: But you couldn't steal signs using technology.
sentences.zh: 但你不能利用技术手段偷暗号。

sentences.en: Frick never actually punished anybody for sign-stealing.
sentences.zh: 弗里克实际上从未因偷暗号惩罚过任何人。

sentences.en: And it took Major League Baseball 40 years to make an official rule about it.
sentences.zh: 而美国职业棒球大联盟花了40年才制定出相关正式规则。

sentences.en: In 2000, they finally banned sign-stealing by electronic means.
sentences.zh: 2000年，他们终于禁止了利用电子手段偷暗号。

sentences.en: They had to do it because technology was moving so quickly at that point.
sentences.zh: 他们必须这样做，因为当时技术发展太快了。

sentences.en: The 2000 rule was meant to stop cell phones from being used to steal signs.
sentences.zh: 2000年的规则旨在阻止手机被用于偷暗号。

sentences.en: But by the early 2010s, baseball clubhouses were filled with video screens.
sentences.zh: 但到了2010年代初，棒球俱乐部的休息室里到处都是视频屏幕。

sentences.en: Some of them were installed by the league itself when they started allowing teams to use
sentences.zh: 其中一些是联盟自己安装的，当时他们开始允许球队使用

sentences.en: video replay to challenge umpires' calls.
sentences.zh: 视频回放来挑战裁判的判罚。

sentences.en: The presence of all these new screens made cheating incredibly tempting.
sentences.zh: 所有这些新屏幕的存在让作弊变得极具诱惑力。

sentences.en: Major League Baseball brought the snake into the Garden of Eden and then were surprised
sentences.zh: 美国职业棒球大联盟把蛇带进了伊甸园，然后当球员们咬下苹果时，

sentences.en: when the players took a bite of the apple.
sentences.zh: 他们却感到惊讶。

sentences.en: After a century of back and forth, by the 2010s, there was finally a clear line in the
sentences.zh: 经过一个世纪的反复博弈，到了2010年代，棒球规则中终于有了

sentences.en: rules of baseball.
sentences.zh: 一条明确的界线。

sentences.en: Sign-stealing using technology was not okay.
sentences.zh: 利用技术手段偷暗号是不被允许的。

sentences.en: But with screens everywhere, it felt like a matter of time before someone crossed that
sentences.zh: 但随着屏幕无处不在，感觉迟早会有人越过那条

sentences.en: line and got caught doing it.
sentences.zh: 界线并被抓个正着。

sentences.en: Before they were winning games and sending opposing pitchers back to the minor leagues, the Houston
sentences.zh: 在他们赢得比赛并将对方投手送回小联盟之前，休斯顿

sentences.en: Astros were one of the worst teams in the history of baseball.
sentences.zh: 太空人队曾是棒球史上最差的球队之一。

sentences.en: Starting in 2011, they lost 100 games three years in a row.
sentences.zh: 从2011年开始，他们连续三年输掉了100场比赛。

sentences.en: Some of their games had local TV ratings of 0.0, which meant that Nielsen couldn't confirm
sentences.zh: 他们的一些比赛在当地的电视收视率为0.0，这意味着尼尔森无法确认

sentences.en: a single Houstonian who watched the games.
sentences.zh: 有任何一个休斯顿人观看了这些比赛。

sentences.en: They earned nicknames like the Lastros and the Disastros, which are pretty good.
sentences.zh: 他们获得了像“Lastros”（输球人）和“Disastros”（灾难人）这样的绰号，还挺贴切的。

sentences.en: To turn things around, the Astros took a page from the Moneyball playbook and hired a
sentences.zh: 为了扭转局面，太空人队借鉴了《点球成金》的策略，雇佣了一

sentences.en: fleet of math nerds.
sentences.zh: 大批数学极客。

sentences.en: They worked on sophisticated algorithms that would help the Astros decide which players
sentences.zh: 他们研究复杂的算法，帮助太空人队决定选拔哪些球员，

sentences.en: to draft and what strategies to execute on the field.
sentences.zh: 以及在场上执行什么策略。

sentences.en: The stats team was called the Nerd Cave.
sentences.zh: 这个数据团队被称为“极客洞穴”。

sentences.en: And so, Ben, you know this because you actually covered the Astros firsthand.
sentences.zh: 所以，本，你知道这一点，因为你亲自报道过太空人队。

sentences.en: Yeah, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我报道过。

sentences.en: So in 2014, I spent a lot of time in the team's front office for a story for Sports Illustrated.
sentences.zh: 2014年，我为了给《体育画报》写一篇报道，在球队管理层待了很长时间。

sentences.en: And when I got there, I found I was really impressed with what I saw.
sentences.zh: 当我到达那里时，我发现自己对所见所闻印象深刻。

sentences.en: I came away convinced that they were on the path to turning things around.
sentences.zh: 我离开时确信他们正走在扭转局面的道路上。

sentences.en: So before the story ran, my editor asked me to estimate the year it's all going to come
sentences.zh: 所以在报道发表前，我的编辑让我预测他们会在哪一年

sentences.en: together.
sentences.zh: 大获成功。

sentences.en: And I gave it my best guess.
sentences.zh: 我给出了我最好的猜测。

sentences.en: So at the end of 2014, the issue containing my piece hit mailboxes across the country with
sentences.zh: 2014年底，刊登我文章的那期杂志寄到了全国各地的信箱，

sentences.en: a cover that reads, you're 2017 World Series champs.
sentences.zh: 封面上写着：你们是2017年世界大赛冠军。

sentences.en: Turns out I was right.
sentences.zh: 事实证明我猜对了。

sentences.en: In October 2017, Mike Bolsinger was sitting at a bar watching the Houston Astros play Game
sentences.zh: 2017年10月，迈克·博辛格正坐在酒吧里观看休斯顿太空人队打世界大赛

sentences.en: 7 of the World Series.
sentences.zh: 第七场比赛。

sentences.en: This was only three months after his final major league game.
sentences.zh: 这距离他最后一场大联盟比赛仅仅过去三个月。

sentences.en: The Astros were playing one of Bolsinger's old teams, the L.A.
sentences.zh: 太空人队当时正在对阵博辛格的老东家之一，洛杉矶

sentences.en: Dodgers.
sentences.zh: 道奇队。

sentences.en: The Dodgers, you know, I love every single one of them.
sentences.zh: 道奇队，你知道的，我爱他们每一个人。

sentences.en: It was the greatest organization that I ever played for them.
sentences.zh: 那是我效力过的最伟大的组织。

sentences.en: So I wanted them to win.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望他们赢。

sentences.en: But you felt the Astros deserved it?
sentences.zh: 但你觉得太空人队理应获胜？

sentences.en: But, oh, I mean, yeah, 100%.
sentences.zh: 但是，噢，我是说，是的，百分之百。

sentences.en: I mean, I think to me they had the better lineup.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得他们有更好的阵容。

sentences.en: It is what it is.
sentences.zh: 事实就是这样。

sentences.en: Mike Bolsinger had mixed emotions about the whole series.
sentences.zh: 迈克·博辛格对整个系列赛心情复杂。

sentences.en: He respected the Astros for their talent.
sentences.zh: 他尊重太空人队的才华。

sentences.en: And baseball fans everywhere were rooting for them.
sentences.zh: 而且各地的棒球迷都在为他们加油。

sentences.en: The Astros weren't just winners.
sentences.zh: 太空人队不仅仅是赢家。

sentences.en: They were likable winners.
sentences.zh: 他们是讨人喜欢的赢家。

sentences.en: They were playing in Houston's second World Series ever.
sentences.zh: 他们正在参加休斯顿历史上第二次世界大赛。

sentences.en: And they made it the same year Hurricane Harvey devastated their home city.
sentences.zh: 而且他们打进决赛的那一年，飓风哈维摧毁了他们的家乡城市。

sentences.en: Their stars, like Jose Altuve and Alex Bregman, were fun to watch.
sentences.zh: 他们的明星球员，比如何塞·奥图维和亚历克斯·布雷格曼，看他们打球很有趣。

sentences.en: It was a real Cinderella story.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个灰姑娘式的励志故事。

sentences.en: The Sports Illustrated cover in 2014.
sentences.zh: 2014年的《体育画报》封面。

sentences.en: And the article by Ben Reeder.
sentences.zh: 还有本·里德的那篇文章。

sentences.en: They nailed it.
sentences.zh: 他们预测准了。

sentences.en: Hey, that's you.
sentences.zh: 嘿，那是你。

sentences.en: Yeah, although they kept pronouncing my name wrong.
sentences.zh: 是的，尽管他们一直把我的名字读错。

sentences.en: Anyhow, the Astros were champions.
sentences.zh: 总之，太空人队是冠军。

sentences.en: If you have a lineup like that, if you're hitting the ball like that,
sentences.zh: 如果你有那样的阵容，如果你能那样击球，

sentences.en: putting up numbers like that,
sentences.zh: 打出那样的数据，

sentences.en: there's no reason why you shouldn't win.
sentences.zh: 没有理由不赢球。

sentences.en: You know, when you have good pitching and you're putting up 10-plus runs a game,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你拥有出色的投手，并且每场比赛能得10分以上时，

sentences.en: it feels like, how can you lose?
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，怎么可能输呢？

sentences.en: Me, Mike Bolsinger, and almost everybody else assumed the Astros took the World Series
sentences.zh: 我和迈克·博辛格，以及几乎所有人都认为太空人队赢下世界大赛，

sentences.en: because of their mix of young talent and the shrewd decision-making from the nerd cave.
sentences.zh: 是因为他们年轻天才的组合以及“极客洞穴”精明的决策。

sentences.en: But two years later, we learned the truth.
sentences.zh: 但两年后，我们得知了真相。

sentences.en: There was a lot more to the story.
sentences.zh: 故事远不止于此。

sentences.en: In late 2019, a whistleblower came forward, a pitcher who had played with the Astros for three seasons.
sentences.zh: 2019年底，一位吹哨人站了出来，他是一位曾在太空人队效力三个赛季的投手。

sentences.en: They have a guy on the record, a guy that was on the team, Mike Fiers, a pitcher, who laid out exactly what they do.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个公开身份的人，一个曾在队里的球员，迈克·法尔斯，一名投手，他详细说明了他们到底做了什么。

sentences.en: Mike Fiers alleged that the Astros had been sign-stealing during their championship season.
sentences.zh: 迈克·法尔斯声称太空人队在他们的夺冠赛季一直在偷暗号。

sentences.en: While the team had these fancy modern algorithms and an entire cave full of data nerds,
sentences.zh: 虽然球队拥有这些先进的现代算法和一整个装满数据极客的洞穴，

sentences.en: their sign-stealing plan was a lot like those used 50 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 但他们的偷暗号计划和50年前使用的方法非常相似。

sentences.en: It was a mix of high-tech tools and low-budget mischief.
sentences.zh: 这是高科技工具和低成本恶作剧的结合。

sentences.en: The Astros had a camera aimed directly at the other team's catcher,
sentences.zh: 太空人队有一台摄像机直接对准对方球队的捕手，

sentences.en: which broadcast to a TV in the tunnel behind the dugout.
sentences.zh: 并将画面传送到休息区后面通道里的电视上。

sentences.en: To communicate the pitch to the batters, Astros players would watch the TV.
sentences.zh: 为了将球路传达给击球手，太空人队的球员会盯着电视看。

sentences.en: And when they saw a fastball coming, they did nothing.
sentences.zh: 当他们看到直球要来时，他们什么都不做。

sentences.en: Any other pitch, they would hit a bat against a plastic garbage can.
sentences.zh: 如果是其他球路，他们就会用球棒敲击塑料垃圾桶。

sentences.en: It sounded like this.
sentences.zh: 听起来是这样的。

sentences.en: Here it is again.
sentences.zh: 再听一遍。

sentences.en: We tried to come up with an analogy for what it sounds like,
sentences.zh: 我们试着找一个比喻来形容它的声音，

sentences.en: but really, it sounds exactly like a bat hitting a plastic garbage can.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，它听起来就像球棒敲击塑料垃圾桶的声音。

sentences.en: Major League Baseball opened a full investigation into the accusations.
sentences.zh: 美国职业棒球大联盟对这些指控展开了全面调查。

sentences.en: The Astros' manager and general manager were suspended and then fired by the team.
sentences.zh: 太空人队的经理和总经理被停职，随后被球队解雇。

sentences.en: The team was fined $5 million, which is not a lot of money for a franchise worth nearly $2 billion.
sentences.zh: 球队被罚款500万美元，对于一家价值近20亿美元的俱乐部来说，这不算什么钱。

sentences.en: The investigation confirmed the Astros had been sign-stealing during the 2017
sentences.zh: 调查证实太空人队在2017年和2018赛季期间，

sentences.en: and 2018 seasons, and during the playoffs, and maybe even the World Series.
sentences.zh: 以及季后赛，甚至可能是世界大赛期间，一直在偷暗号。

sentences.en: The Astros are still the 2017 World Series champions,
sentences.zh: 太空人队依然是2017年世界大赛的冠军，

sentences.en: even though many baseball fans insist they deserve a massive asterisk.
sentences.zh: 尽管许多棒球迷坚持认为他们应该被打上一个巨大的星号。

sentences.en: Some of the game's biggest stars think that too, like Aaron Judge of the Yankees.
sentences.zh: 一些棒球界最大的明星也这么认为，比如洋基队的阿隆·贾奇。

sentences.en: I just don't think it holds any value with them.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这对他们来说没有任何价值。

sentences.en: You know, you cheated and you didn't earn it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你作弊了，你赢得并不光彩。

sentences.en: You know, that's how I feel.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是我的感受。

sentences.en: And Mike Trout, the best player in baseball.
sentences.zh: 还有迈克·特劳特，棒球界最好的球员。

sentences.en: It's sad for baseball.
sentences.zh: 这对棒球来说很可悲。

sentences.en: You know, it's tough.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很难受。

sentences.en: You know, they cheated.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们作弊了。

sentences.en: And, you know, just I don't agree with the punishment.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我不同意这个惩罚。

sentences.en: The Astros' scandals created many what-ifs that can never be answered.
sentences.zh: 太空人队的丑闻制造了许多永远无法回答的“如果”。

sentences.en: No one denies that the Astros were a really talented team.
sentences.zh: 没有人否认太空人队是一支非常有天赋的球队。

sentences.en: But would they still be World Series champions if they hadn't cheated?
sentences.zh: 但如果他们没有作弊，他们还会是世界大赛冠军吗？

sentences.en: Data analysts have tried to answer that question,
sentences.zh: 数据分析师们试图回答这个问题，

sentences.en: and several prominent ones have found the advantage the Astros got from sign-stealing
sentences.zh: 几位著名的分析师发现，太空人队从偷暗号中获得的优势，

sentences.en: might have been surprisingly small.
sentences.zh: 可能小得令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Of course, a small advantage can mean a lot in such a competitive sport.
sentences.zh: 当然，在如此激烈的运动中，微小的优势可能意味着很多。

sentences.en: These questions aren't so abstract for someone like Mike Bolsinger.
sentences.zh: 对于像迈克·博辛格这样的人来说，这些问题并不那么抽象。

sentences.en: An analysis by a computer programmer revealed that when the Astros faced Bolsinger,
sentences.zh: 一位计算机程序员的分析显示，当太空人队面对博辛格时，

sentences.en: they banged on their trash can lid 54 times.
sentences.zh: 他们敲击垃圾桶盖子多达54次。

sentences.en: The most times the Astros had used that system in all of 2017.
sentences.zh: 这是太空人队在整个2017年使用该系统次数最多的一次。

sentences.en: And a lot of those bangs happened during Bolsinger's short appearance in the game.
sentences.zh: 而且其中很多敲击声都发生在博辛格短暂上场期间。

sentences.en: Someone hit the trash can immediately before 12 of his 29 pitches.
sentences.zh: 在他29次投球中的12次之前，有人立即敲击了垃圾桶。

sentences.en: It just makes you mad.
sentences.zh: 这真的会让你很生气。

sentences.en: It thinks, you know, what would have happened if I hadn't pitched that game?
sentences.zh: 它会让你想，你知道的，如果我当初没投那场球会怎样？

sentences.en: So then you start to question things about your career now,
sentences.zh: 于是你开始质疑自己现在的职业生涯，

sentences.en: and then it truly was the most embarrassing moment in my career.
sentences.zh: 那确实是我职业生涯中最尴尬的时刻。

sentences.en: I've never been more embarrassed myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己从未感到如此尴尬。

sentences.en: Ever.
sentences.zh: 从来没有。

sentences.en: Mike Bolsinger filed a legal complaint against the Astros on February 10, 2020.
